frames: I saw or felt ____ when the drum was tapped.
When we stopped the drum top, ____.
We tried again. I noticed ____.
My picture shows ____. I still want to check ____.

parallelExample.context: A teacher gently plucks the end of a ruler held on a table.
parallelExample.move: Compare it while it moves and after it stops. Tell or show what you notice. Try again gently.
parallelExample.whyItHelps: You compare before and after on one object. Use that idea for the drum.

frames: In this place, I found these kinds: ____.
Both places had ____. Only one showed ____.
We looked for the same time. We noticed ____.
Our search may have missed ____ because ____.

parallelExample.context: Two photos show small parts of a pond edge and a lawn.
parallelExample.move: List the kinds you can see in each. Count kinds, not just how many living things there are. Name something the photos might miss.
parallelExample.whyItHelps: The photos help you practice the same kind of comparison. A photo or short search cannot show everything.

frames: The rock changed in place when ____. That is ____.
The material moved from ____ to ____. That shows ____.
We changed ____, but kept ____ the same.
Our repeated results suggest ____. Our tray cannot show ____.

parallelExample.context: Another class compares how packed and loose soil affect runoff in small trays.
parallelExample.move: They change how tightly the soil is packed. They keep tray slope, soil amount and water input alike. They repeat the comparison and measure sediment the same way.
parallelExample.whyItHelps: The factor differs from your slope test, but the need to control other conditions and repeat measurements is the same.

frames: I wrote ____ as ____ so the places line up.
In the ____ place, ____ is greater than ____.
Both models use the same whole: ____.
More decimal digits do not always mean more because ____.

parallelExample.context: Two jugs hold 0.4 L and 0.35 L.
parallelExample.move: Write 0.4 as 0.40. Compare 40 hundredths with 35 hundredths of the same liter. Explain why the extra zero did not add any liquid.
parallelExample.whyItHelps: Matching units and places lets you compare values instead of counting digits. Use that method for the ribbons.

frames: Our model gives red a probability of ____ because ____.
We returned and mixed each counter so ____.
In ____ trials, red appeared ____ times. Its relative frequency was ____.
The trial results differ from the model by ____. This does not guarantee that ____.

parallelExample.context: A different bag has two green and two yellow counters of the same size and shape.
parallelExample.move: Assuming each counter is equally likely, green has probability 2/4. Compare that model with repeated draws, replacing and mixing each counter. A set of trials need not be exactly half green.
parallelExample.whyItHelps: It separates a model probability from an observed relative frequency. Use the same distinction for your three-blue, one-red bag.
